what: The modem seizes the line but never dials - observed 2026-09-07, unresolved

observed.by ear: dial tone only; no DTMF digits heard, and the operator confirmed the call never dialled
observed.ATDT9099: no result code for 60 s, then NO CARRIER (the S7 timeout)
observed.ATDT under X4: no NO DIALTONE inside 25 s - which under X4 means the modem believes it has dial tone
observed.ATDP9099: no result code in 30 s either - pulse dialling fails the same way
observed.ATI11: answers with live link diagnostics, so the DSP is responding to the supervisor
observed.AT&V: ERROR - not supported by this ID_SDL build

reading: The modem goes off hook and holds the line, and then emits nothing in either dialling mode. Tone dialling is generated by the DSP (docs/driving-the-tones.md: the supervisor's dialer folds each dial-string character to a keypad index and sends it as a mailbox tag), so a wedged DSP would explain the tone case - but pulse dialling failing the same way points at the dialer sequencer rather than tone generation alone.
what this session did that could be resp: Repeated DSP resets and downloads of foreign kernels into DSP program RAM by the takeover probes.
Several AT&T8 self-tests terminated by sending CR rather than exited cleanly.
A placement at 0x1a00 that needlessly zeroed a live firmware data block at 0x1aab-0x1ad6.
Everything above is RAM, so a power cycle clears all of it. ATZ does not - it reloads the stored profile without re-downloading the DSP.
honest caveat: This modem was never asked to dial before this session, so there is no baseline. It is not established that dialling ever worked on this unit, and the fault may predate everything here.
next: Bypass the dialer and command the DSP to make a tone directly: the dial path is six mailbox messages (0x16 start, 0x19/0x1a/0x1b constants, 0x13 keypad index, 0x16 stop) and courier_emu.dsp_mailbox already sends that shape, confirmed on hardware in artifacts/dsp-mailbox-command-02. That isolates DSP tone generation from the dialer completely. Note docs/driving-the-tones.md is written against DSP 3.0.13 and says explicitly it should not be run as written against the board's 3.1.2.

after power cycle (2026-09-07).who: operator power cycled the unit after the first attempts
after power cycle (2026-09-07).pulse: ATDP produces audible relay clicks - the operator heard them, though was unsure the count was right
after power cycle (2026-09-07).tone: ATDT9099 with X4 and T set still produces no DTMF and no result code in 45 s
after power cycle (2026-09-07).conclusion: The DTMF failure SURVIVES a cold power cycle, so it is not caused by this session's DSP resets, kernel downloads, interrupted &T8 tests or the stray write at 0x1aab. Pulse dialling works, so the DAA, the hook relay and the dialer sequencer are fine. What does not work is tone generation, which is the DSP's job.

S-registers: not the problem.verdict: All defaults. S11 - the DTMF tone duration - is 070 ms, which is normal; S6 (wait before blind dial) 2 s, S7 (wait for carrier) 60 s matching the observed timeout, S8 (comma pause) 2 s. Nothing here would suppress DTMF.

two non-S settings worth noting.DIAL=PULSE: the default dial method is pulse, which ATDT should override per call and evidently does not fix
two non-S settings worth noting.X1: extended result codes but no dial tone or busy detection, so the modem blind dials after S6 - this is why no NO DIALTONE is ever reported, and it is expected behaviour rather than a fault
